## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag should read its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because the project's CLI flag rules require an environment default for every flag added under `cli/`. This review found no other defect in the exclusion logic, its tests, or the docs row.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to `cli/main.py` that makes `collect()` skip files whose base name matches any pattern. It also adds a row to `docs/flags.md`, five tests in `tests/test_main.py`, and a new fixture file `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — Running `archive src` with `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'` set and no `--exclude` archives the `.log` files, because the flag hardcodes `default=[]`. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable (for `--dry-run`, `ARCHIVE_DRY_RUN`), because CI sets options through the environment." — CI jobs that set exclusions through the environment silently archive files they meant to skip. — Fix: Decide how one `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` value carries several globs (for example a separator), then document it in `docs/flags.md` and add a test in `tests/test_main.py`.
